title: Teachers protest union dissolution and forced retirement at parliament
threshold_50_evidence: Hundreds explicitly reported; no exact numeric bound created.

start_date.summary: January 3 explicitly identified as actual sit-in.

location.summary: Assembly in parliament vicinity; police pushed participants into opposite square.

scope.summary: Specific Amman parliament gathering, not a verified national multi-location action.

organizer.summary: Attribution of formal call unresolved; no organizer assigned.

demands.summary: Reverse forced early retirements and dissolution of teachers' union; own-state employment and political-process demands.

participants_original.summary: Both reports explicitly say hundreds; no precise numeric bounds invented.

state_accommodation.summary: Delegation actually entered and met parliamentary education committee and MPs; success not assumed.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: Police physically pushed teachers to square opposite parliament.

end_date.summary: Physical end not established; null retained.

protester_violence.summary: No sufficiently explicit description establishing presence or absence of protester violence.

state_other_responses.summary: December31 detention background not assigned to January3. Batons mentioned in S002 later section have unclear date attribution; other six responses remain unknown.

notes: Discrete January 3 assembly against Jordanian governmental forced retirements and court dissolution of the teachers' union. Source reporting of hundreds establishes size qualitatively. December 28 march is a prior discrete action, not evidence of continuous occupation across New Year. January 10 recurring rally retained separately for episode review. Actual delegation meeting with MPs supports accommodation without assuming victory. No physical end demonstrated.
open_questions: Should January 3 and January 10 recurring Sunday actions be one protest phase under original unit rules? No continuous assembly is established.
Formal organizer: S006 describes general assembly mobilization; S002 interview says union board did not issue a formal call.

title: Teachers regroup near parliament after police prevention
location: King Abdullah I mosque, Abdali parking and nearby streets, Amman
participants_original: Dozens in regrouped gatherings; estimates of100 versus200–250 detainees concern custody, not crowd.

start_date.summary: Actual Sunday January10 action reported retrospectively.

location.summary: King Abdullah I mosque, Abdali parking and nearby streets.

organizer.summary: Interview denies formal board call; formal organizer unresolved.

demands.summary: Support teachers' union and oppose forced retirement and dissolution.

participants_original.summary: Dozens in smaller regrouped gatherings; separate detention estimates100 and200–250 not crowd size.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither read source establishes at least50 simultaneously assembled.

state_arrests.summary: Teachers and others detained briefly and released.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: Orders to leave, pursuit and breakup of regrouped participants.

end_date.summary: Calloff and releases reported; physical end remains unproven.

protester_violence.summary: Rights group's peaceful framing not used to infer absence of all protester violence.

state_other_responses.summary: No confidently event-attributed evidence for accommodation, beatings, ignore, killings or shootings; retained unknown.

notes: Actual January 10 gatherings around Abdali after prevention of access to parliament. Eyewitness reporting describes dozens regrouping; detention-hall count100 and estimate200–250 detainees cannot establish a simultaneous crowd of50. Separate recurring Sunday phase retained for review. Police orders to leave and pursuit/breakup support dispersal; brief detentions support arrests. Public declaration ending the stand is not treated as observed physical end.
open_questions: Find a contemporaneous simultaneous assembled crowd estimate; do not use cumulative detentions.
Resolve January3/10 phase boundary and formal organizer.
Unclear date attribution of baton allegation; beatings stays unknown.

title: Dhiban evening march supporting teachers and opposing corruption

scope.summary: Reported local march; national coordination unresolved.

demands.summary: Teacher-union solidarity and rejection of corruption.

state_response.summary: All seven responses unknown; report silence not absence.

notes: Actual Thursday evening march after Maghrib in Dhiban supports teachers and rejects corruption. Domestic public demands are clear; crowd size and formal link to national teacher mobilization are unverified. Not merged with the unemployed Dhiban tent merely because location overlaps.
open_questions: Determine whether local solidarity march belongs to an organized national action or a separate local unit.

location.summary: Outside Agriculture Ministry; opened report does not explicitly identify city.

demands.summary: Farm-policy and credit-interest grievances directed to government.

state_accommodation.summary: Minister actually met farmers and heard demands.

state_other_responses.summary: Other six responses unknown; no inference from silence.

organizer.summary: Actual report does not establish formal organizer; announcement lead not used as proof.

notes: Actual January10 public gathering. Demands concern migrant agricultural labor, marketing and minimum crop prices, and agricultural-credit interest relief. Agriculture Minister Muhammad Dawoudia actually met farmers; next-day five-person committee meeting is prospective and not coded as executed. JordanTimes and February2 AmmanNet leads remain blocked and cannot independently establish details.

Check whether February farmer actions are later discrete phases or a continuous occupation; opened source establishes no end.
